script.cite: BK2 printed p.7 = book2-3-4.pdf PDF p.13, step 1
script.quote: Turn the DECIMAL INPUT-OUTPUT knob to number 4 and push pushbutton 5. This transmits the number "four" to the computer. Relay light 4 comes ON to indicate that a "four" is being stored.

script.cite: BK2 printed p.7 = book2-3-4.pdf PDF p.13, step 1
script.quote: Relay light 4 comes ON to indicate that a "four" is being stored. Data has been communicated from the operator to MINIVAC 601 by turning the DECIMAL INPUT-OUTPUT knob to the desired number and by instructing the computer to remember the selected number by pushing pushbutton 5.

script.cite: BK2 printed p.7 = book2-3-4.pdf PDF p.13, step 2
script.quote: Push pushbutton 6 and release. This action instructs the computer to forget all previous data, and relay light 4 goes OFF.

note: Wire list image-read from the 300 dpi page; 23 connections, no errata entry for this page. Pushbuttons are pressed and released as separate steps. The dial is turned by hand to D4 (90 degrees, 22.5-degree pitch) before pushbutton 5 is pressed; no dial assertion is made because the page gives the knob position only as an instruction. The second expect (light 4 still ON after pushbutton 5 is released) rests on 'is being stored' and on step 2, which says light 4 goes OFF on pushbutton 6 and so presupposes it is ON until then. Not asserted: the other relay lights (the page never says they stay OFF), and the open-ended 'select another number yourself (between 1 and 5)' trial (no stated observable for any specific number).
